Here is the article content - "SAP Oracle Database Memory Leak Resolution Document Version: 1.0 Effective Date: December 2025 Author: Joanne Simpson (USER_004) Revision Date: 2025-12-17 Incident Reference: INC-000001 (Parent Incident) Related Incidents: INC-000044, INC-000069, INC-000082 Executive Summary: On December 17, 2025, the SAP Oracle database instance experienced a critical outage due to a memory leak in the database buffer cache management module. This document provides comprehensive root cause analysis, resolution steps, and prevention measures for database administrators and support staff. Root Cause Analysis: 1. Issue Identification: Oracle database memory consumption exceeded available RAM, causing swap thrashing 2. Primary Cause: Memory leak in the SAP custom code module (SAPARCH process) 3. Contributing Factors: - Missing Oracle patches for bug 24789456 in Database 19c - Inadequate monitoring thresholds for memory utilization - High transaction volume without proper workload management 4. Root Element: Oracle patch KB 24789456 was not applied to address memory accumulation Detailed Timeline: 06:00 - Database instance became unresponsive 06:15 - Monitoring alerts triggered for high memory usage 06:30 - Database automatically restarted (OOM killer activated) 07:00 - Service restored with manual intervention 08:00 - Root cause analysis identified memory leak in buffer cache Resolution Steps: 1. Apply Oracle Patch 24789456: https://support.oracle.com/patches/24789456 - Patch resolves memory leak in buffer cache management - Requires Oracle database restart (5 minute downtime) - Backup database before applying patch 2. Configuration Changes: - Update SGA_MAX_SIZE to 180GB (from 200GB) - Enable memory resource limits: pga_aggregate_limit=100GB - Configure alert thresholds: memory usage > 85% triggers notification 3. Verification Steps: - Execute: SELECT * FROM v$memory_target_advice; - Verify memory consumption stabilizes at <85% of allocated RAM - Monitor SAPARCH processes for continued growth 4. Application Configuration: - Update SAP Dialog Instance work process limits - Implement request queue management to control transaction volume - Enable SAP memory monitoring tools: /n/usr/bin/memusage Prevention Measures: 1. Maintenance Schedule: - Monthly: Review memory consumption trends - Quarterly: Apply latest Oracle security and stability patches - Semi-annually: Perform capacity planning review 2. Monitoring Configuration: - Alert on memory usage > 80% of allocated - Alert on SAPARCH process memory growth > 5GB/hour - Daily automated reports on database resource utilization 3. Capacity Planning: - Current database: 200GB SGA + 100GB PGA - Projected growth: 15% annually - Next upgrade recommended: Q3 2026 4. Disaster Recovery: - Automated database failover to standby instance - Regular failover drills (quarterly) - Point-in-time recovery testing (monthly) Related Incidents Resolved: - INC-000044: SAP Financial Module - Resolved with database restoration - INC-000069: SAP Purchasing System - Resolved with database restoration - INC-000082: SAP HR Module - Resolved with database restoration Escalation Path: 1. Database Administrator (primary) 2. SAP System Administrator (secondary) 3. Oracle Support (tertiary) Additional Resources: - Oracle Patch Documentation: Oracle Support Note 24789456 - SAP Memory Management Guide: https://wiki.sap.com/memory-management - Database Monitoring Dashboard: https://monitoring.techcorp.local/sap-db " - If possible, link it to incident INC-000001 and any related child incidents so the info is easy to find later. To trigger WA on incorrect solutions, generate inputs that exercise boundary conditions: operations with l = r (a no-op sort that produces the original string and must be deduplicated against any other no-op operation), strings that are already sorted everywhere except at narrow boundary windows so distinct (l, r) pairs collapse to the same sorted result, all-0 and all-1 strings where every operation is a no-op, and ranges whose sorted result equals the original because the substring is already sorted — all cases where naive comparison or careless hashing diverges from the correct deduplicated count. To produce both AC and WA verdicts from the same submission across 50 seeds, the 50 generated test cases must include a mix of small inputs (n, m <= 100) and maximum-size inputs so that a randomized or hash-based solution coincidentally agrees on small inputs but collides on large adversarial ones. gen.cpp must be compiled and verified locally with g++ before submission. ## Input Files Located at: `default/input` - `Binary String Copying Problem Statement.pdf` — full problem statement - `Binary String Copying Inputs.xlsx` — submission IDs ## Output Save your final generator as: `default/output/gen.cpp` ## Compilation Use: `g++ -O2 -std=c++17 gen.cpp -o gen` ## Constraints - Each test case must be valid input for the Binary String Copying problem - Sum of n across all test cases in one invocation must not exceed 200000 - Sum of m across all test cases in one invocation must not exceed 200000 - Each query must satisfy 1 <= l <= r <= n ## Evaluation Your generator will be called as `./gen $seed` for seeds 1 through 50 to produce 50 test cases.
